[Rumor] Bocoran Intel Nova Lake-S: Core Ultra 9 4970K BFC 28 Core, Turbo 5,5 GHz, Cache 144 MB — 7 SKU Terungkap

The newly leaked spec sheet details crucial information on the upcoming Intel Nova Lake-S processors, including the 28-core bLLC variant. We have been reporting on the Nova Lake-S for months now, and we previously published posts detailing some of the high-end SKUs in the lineup. Our coverage mostly included the Intel Core Ultra 9 4970K and the Core Ultra 7 4870K , which are among the handful of bLLC variants with additional cache, aimed at competing against AMD's X3D chips. We also reported on one or two more SKUs, like the Intel Core Ultra 5 4650K, and the latest report confirms the previously reported specifications. Thanks to Videocardz for getting their hands on the Intel document that contained information on seven Nova Lake-S desktop processors. The outlet claims that the document listed CPUs based on the C1 stepping qualification samples, and it's likely that the final products will arrive with the mentioned specifications. According to the document, the Intel Core Ultra 9 4970K BFC 28-core variant will get 144 MB of LLC (Last Level Cache), and the other one with the same cache size will be the Intel Core Ultra 7 4870K BFC. Only the Core Ultra 9 4900 BFC will have a slightly reduced LLC cache of 120 MB . However, it's a low-power variant with a 65W TDP rating. The rest of the stack has a default TDP rating of 125W . The Core Ultra 9 4970K BFC can boost to 5.5 GHz , and the non-BFC Core Ultra 9 4950K can reach 5.4 GHz and features just 36 MB of L3 cache. The Core Ultra 5 series processors, including the Core Ultra 5 4650K and the KF variants, will feature 22-core configurations (6+12+4), paired with 30 MB of L3 cache, and up to 5.1 GHz P-Core Turbo clock. Videocardz says all the processors support DDR5-8000 memory, which is a substantial upgrade over DDR5-6400 support on Arrow Lake-S processors. It will be interesting to see how much of all of this will contribute to the gaming scene, as previously we reported that some chips can deliver up to 20% higher gaming performance vs. the Arrow Lake-S .
